heros.infro: William the 1st was the Duke of Normandy and later King of England. He invaded England with an army in 1066. At the Battle of Hastings, he defeated Harold Godwinson, this along with other revolts is known as the Norman Conquest. This was the last time England was conquered by a foreign power. As King of England he was responsible for the Doomsday Book, precursor to the modern census.  He died at age of 59 in 1087.
heros.name: William the Conqueror

heros.infro: Charlemagne, or Charles the Great, is a figure larger than life. At seven feet tall, he was as large as… He was a devout Christian king and mighty conqueror, whose rule helped define the shape and character of medieval Europe. He subjugated the Saxons and other tribes in Germany, making conquests in Spain and Italy, as well as ruling over France in his quest for the title of Emperor of the West. In Rome, Pope Leo III crowned him with the imperial crown worn by the old emperors of the Roman Empire. Charlemagne is credited with implementing important governmental, fiscal, ecclesiastical and cultural reforms.
heros.name: Charlemagne

heros.infro: Roman historian who wrote a monumental history of Rome, Ab Urbe Condita, from its founding through the reign of Augustus in Livy's own time.
heros.name: Livy

heros.infro: Biographer of the Greek philosophers, is supposed by some to have received his surname from the town of Laerte in Cilicia, Asia Minor, and by others from the Roman family of the Laertii.
heros.name: Diogenes Laertios

heros.infro: Ben Jonson fought the Spaniards in Flanders, returned to England and joined an acting company, and was a member of the Lord Chamberlain's company with William Shakespeare. Human nature fascinated both playwrights, but Jonson specialized in satires like Volpone ("The Fox"). He also wrote masques and poetry, and his fellow writers esteemed him as "O Rare Ben Jonson".
heros.name: Ben Jonson

heros.infro: Known as the Eagle of Brittany, was a Breton knight and French military commander during theHundred Years War. He was Constable of France from 1370 to his death.
heros.name: Bertrand Du Guesclin

heros.infro: Eratosthenes (276  - 194 B.C.) was a Greek mathemetician born in Cyrene which is now in Libya, North Africa. His teachers included the scholar Lysanias of Cyrene and the philosopher Ariston of Chios who had studied under Zeno, the founder of the Stoic school of philosophy.  Eratosthenes also studied under the poet and scholar Callimachus  then spent some years studying in Athens.  He is best known for his work on prime numbers and for measuring the diameter of the earth but made many other major contributions to the progress of science.
heros.name: Erastosthenes

heros.infro: Named Pope in 1503, Julius II established a strong papacy that was independent of Italian nobles, notably Cesare Borgia, and restored and enlarged the Papal States. He established the Holy League in 1510 in opposition to the French who were forced out of Italy in 1512. Julius II also dispatched missionaries to Africa, India, and the Americas and was a patron of the arts and artists including Michelangelo and Raphael.
heros.name: Guiliano della Rovere, Pope Julius II

heros.infro: Baldwin I of Edessa was a leader of the First Crusade and was an important figure in the capture of Jerusalem in 1099 being named King of Jerusalem  soon after it fell.  He was an aggressive ruler, leading several campaigns between 1101 and 1115 to expand the limits of his kingdom capturing important cities in the region such as Acre and Tripoli.  After his death in 1118 William Tyre described as being "expert in the use of arms, agile on horseback [as well as] active and diligent whenever the affairs of the realm called him."
heros.name: Baldwin I of Edessa

heros.infro: Known as Máel Coluim mac Domnaill (anglicised to Malcolm I) became king of Scots when his cousin abdicated to become a monk. Malcom was known to raid Moray, Northumbria as far south as the Tees, and battle various foreigners.
heros.name: Malcolm I of Scotland

heros.infro: Louis the Stammerer ruled in Aquitaine and West Francia during the 9th Century.  He had two sons, Louis and Carloman, who would later become Kings of France, but he held the title of King for less than two years.  Louis was said to be physically weak but to his credit we has called "a simple and sweet man, a lover of peace, jjujstice and religion" by contemporaries.  His political impact was relatively minor but he did launch a campaign against the Vikings before his death in 879 when his Kingdom was split between his two sons.
heros.name: Louis the Stammerer

heros.infro: Trader and explorer from the Venetian Republic who gained fame for his worldwide travels. He was one of the first Westerners to travel the Silk Road to China and visit Kublai Khan.
heros.name: Marco Polo

heros.infro: Brian mac Cennétig was called Brian Bóruma or Brian Boru. Leader of the Dal Cais dynasty, he made himself king of Munster and subjugated Leinster in Southern Ireland. After overthrowing the Uú Néill dynasty that had reigned over most of Ireland for 300 years, Boru became the last High King of Ireland in 1011. In the 1014 battle of Clontarf when his army fought the armies of Dublin, Leinster, and Norse settlers, Brian Boru was slain although his forces won the day.
heros.name: Brian Boru

heros.infro: Lothair III was a powerful and very successful ruler of Saxon descent.  He gained the title of Holy Roman Emperor,in part through a very amicable and beneficial relationship with Pope Innocent II.  His most important long-term contribution to the history of the Germanic lands was in his maintenance of the neglected areas of Saxony in the Northeast where he appointed a number of capable Dukes and lesser magistrates who governed the region effectively.
heros.name: Lothair III, Holy Roman Emperor

heros.infro: Wartislaw III was a Griffin duke of Pomerania-Demmin. Wartislaw successfully stopped a Danish invasion in 1234. In the North, Wartislaw was able to expand his sphere of influence up to the Ryck river into the territory of Hilda. Since he did not produce any children from his marriage, Pomerania-Demmin ceased to exist with his death.
heros.name: Wartislaw III, Duke of Pomerania

heros.infro: Roger de Montgomerie, one of William the Conqueror's principal counselors, was granted the title of Earl of Shrewsbury in 1071 and was charged with the rule of Shropshire, a region to the West of modern day Birmingham making him one of the most powerful magnates in all of England at the time.  His mandate was to prevent Welsh incursions into English lands.
heros.name: Earl of Shrewsbury

heros.infro: Raja Raja Cholal was a great emperor of the Tamil Chola Empire in India. He conquered southern India as far as Sri Lanka and Kalinga to the North. He divided the country into districts to help the administration and built the Brihadisvara Temple and enabled wealth distribution.
heros.name: Raja Raja Cholal

heros.infro: Hungry for power, Sforza became the Duke of Milan by seizing power from the rightful heir to the crown after the assassination of his brother Galeazzo.  Although his methods may be less than honorable, Sforza is a firm but able leader.
heros.name: Ludovico Sforza

heros.infro: Eric IV was king of Denmark from 1241 until his death. His rule is known for bitter conflicts and civil wars against his brothers. At the same time Erik faced trouble from the religious orders who insisted that they were immune from taxes that Erik wanted to assess. Erik wanted the church lands taxed as any other landholder would be. He fought constant wars in an attempt to impose more and more taxes on more and more people.
heros.name: Eric IV of Denmark

heros.infro: First husband of Lucrezia Borgia, Sforza was a member of the House of Sforza which ruled Italy.
heros.name: Giovanni Sforza
